Every Porchlight field is listed in `docs/ANIMATION_TODO.md` ("How to use it in an episode JSON"). Built so far: beats without Riot (`riot_optional`), the painted sets (`lake`, `lake_night`, `stoop_sunset`, `stoop_night`, `apartment`, `hall`) with named seats, walking on/off and between spots, the porch-light ending, the lo-fi bed and theme motif, the intro title, storms, chats, fades and letterbox, set life and set lighting. The JSON is checked before rendering (names, moves, cameras, fx), so a typo stops with a message instead of a broken render. Since the Ep 2 review (8 Nov) it also stops on someone back on screen after walking off, a `wal
- Riot's family lives in town. Riot and Rocco share an apartment, with no special meaning.
- The porch light is on Riot and Rocco's apartment building: a small front stoop with an old porch light Riot took from grandpa's house.

- Shorts before the premiere: no build-up at all. ~~Shorts keep their current sets until the premiere and only use Maple Hollow afterwards~~ **Changed 12 Nov 2026 (user): Shorts may use the generic painted sets now** (lake, lake_night, park, main_street, town_square, apartment, stoop_sunset, stoop_night, hall, hall_outside) via `make.py --set`; never the story rooms (bash_home, pip_home, pip_garage, classroom, brook_porch), still no series hints, plot or new characters.

- New side characters approved: the owl teacher ("summer homework"), Pip's parents (make the move a real family situation), Bash's loud family (where his need to prove himself comes from), Lord Puddles the apartment frog, the Mayor as lovably indecisive (complications, never a serious villain). Introduce them gradually, not all in the opening episodes.

- Episode 1: apartment (Bash and Pip on the sofa, Rocco asleep on the beanbag), stoop (Riot sitting on the step under the porch light, Lord Puddles beside him), lake (Riot inside the tower, Rocco on the sand). Stills before the next render.

Rocco has seen Riot leave during the storm and said nothing.

- **Hook (arc end):** the storm passes. In the haunted house, Riot's flashlight lights the table we saw in ep 1. We still don't see what's on it, only his face: exhausted, determined. He whispers, "Again." Cut to the apartment: Rocco, awake in the dark, waiting for him to come home. The porch light clicks off.

sources.excerpt: | **Riot & Rocco's apartment** | Small, messy, cozy. Front stoop with **the porch light** (taken from grandpa's house). Game nights happen here. |

The old porch light from grandpa's house, now on Riot and Rocco's stoop. **On = game night tonight.** Every episode ends with it clicking off, then a small Friendzy logo. In the finale it's the same click, but autumn leaves fall through its last glow.
- The porch light is on Riot and Rocco's apartment building: a small front stoop with an old porch light Riot took from grandpa's house.

- Still 16, final image: approved. In Ep 40 only, the ending is framed close on the porch light and holds about 4 seconds before the click. An autumn stoop repaint is planned (`GEMINI_BATCH.md` 42, 43).

- Episode 1: apartment (Bash and Pip on the sofa, Rocco asleep on the beanbag), stoop (Riot sitting on the step under the porch light, Lord Puddles beside him), lake (Riot inside the tower, Rocco on the sand). Stills before the next render.

- Ep 6 script, staging only (no dialogue changed except one word): "NAME stands at the <spot>" for every gym scene (Mayor on the stage, the boys presenting from the floor, townsfolk at the sides, Hal in the aisle); the chair-stacking part is its own scene `== Stacking chairs | gym | bash, hal` (Riot, Pip and Rocco had walked off); the dead holds became silent reactions + 2 s holds (after the snore; Mrs. Brook now actually exits left and Pip watches; Riot nods at the end); moves added: Riot points / facepalms in the cold open, Rocco shrugs / munches on the stoop; Riot carries his phone in the Big Hal scene too; Hal's "those trees thirty years"

- **Emotional beat:** after everyone leaves, Riot sits on the stoop under the porch light. He touches the old brass fitting for a second. Walt's voice in his head (a short memory line): "That light was on every game night your grandpa ever had." No joke after.
- **Emotional beat:** Pip reads his essay out loud to the boys on the stoop. It's about them. Nobody makes a joke.
| Small emotional beat each episode | Stoop and porch light; Pip beside Bash; Pip's essay; "Then we keep it"; "He'd have liked your friends". |
- **Cold open:** Riot rehearsing a speech to Lord Puddles the frog on the stoop. Lord Puddles leaves mid-sentence.

- **Emotional beat:** Bash, sitting on the stoop afterwards: "Why does it matter so much?" Pip: "Because you keep trying." Bash: "That's not the same as winning." Pip: "Isn't it?" (Seeds Bash's arc; it doesn't resolve it.)

- **Emotional beat:** they walk Riot home without talking. At the stoop, Pip says the first brave thing he's said all season: "You don't have to do everything by yourself, you know." Riot: "Yeah, I do." The porch light is on. Nobody plays a game.

- **Ep 37 "One Small Game" (Slice).** Possibly the last game night on the stoop. Nobody's trying very hard. Bash wins a game of Alias and doesn't notice until Bea tells him. **Beat:** "Huh." He just smiles and passes the chips, to Rocco. At the end, Pip matches the chime paper to the lantern frame, and the blurred face in the photo to Preston.

Riot, a 20-year-old fox lifeguard, has spent years sneaking into the town's "haunted house" to finish his grandfather's old board game alone, without telling anyone. With his roommate Rocco and their younger friends Bash and Pip, a summer of game nights, dumb plans and small mysteries slowly turns into the discovery that the game is holding the whole town in one endless summer. In Maple Hollow, a small lake-and-forest town of animals, it has been summer for decades and nobody has noticed. Riot, a 20-year-old fox lifeguard, has spent years sneaking into the town's "haunted house" to finish his grandfather's old board game alone, without telling anyone. With his roommate Rocco and their younger friends Bash and Pip, a summer of game nights, dumb plans and small mysteries slowly turns into the discovery that the game is holding the whole town in one endless summer. It can only be finished together. Finishing it means autumn arrives, and with it, Pip moves away.

1. Maple Hollow loves board games; they bring generations together. Every summer the town held a **festival** built around one big game played outdoors by the lake.

3. The festival game is old and special: it **keeps the town's memories**. Its board is a map of Maple Hollow; its pieces stand for people, places and events. Each festival, when the round ends and the **last lantern** is released over the lake, that summer becomes a memory the game keeps, and the season moves on.

- **The haunted house** (the old festival hall) is where everything was stored after the storm. The game's magic leaks out there: chairs arrange themselves like a board, a die falls from nowhere, footsteps move in turns, fragments of the storm night replay. It holds **echoes of a night that happened elsewhere** (at the lake). It's evidence, not the cause. Sometimes only one boy sees an echo and has to convince the others.
- **The box:** an old wooden case, hand-painted lid of the lake at dusk, grandpa's initials scratched inside.

- **The board:** a hand-painted map of Maple Hollow (lake in the middle, forest, main street, the park, the hall). The painted town quietly matches the real one, including things built after the storm. This is a late clue (the board "keeps" the town).
- **Lanterns:** 12 small paper lantern markers, one per round. Eleven sit in the "released" slot over the painted lake. **The twelfth slot is empty.**

- **The magic stays subtle all season**, with two big visible moments: **ep 20** (the house replays the storm night in full and the boys see the lake-side game: the twist) and **the finale** (the last lantern rises and the real lake fills with light).

- The four boys take the four seats. Mrs. Brook brings the last lantern she kept. The town gathers at the lake to watch and play along (the crowd round), getting together through Friendzy rooms, which is a natural app moment and not magic.

An animated story series set in Maple Hollow, a lake-and-forest town where summer never ends. Riot, Rocco, Bash and Pip (the Friendzy cast) are the main characters. 40 episodes of 3–4 minutes, landscape, released Wednesday and Saturday.

**By the end of ep 5 the audience knows:** the four boys and their dynamic, the lake, the apartment and the porch light, the "haunted" house, Mrs. Brook, Preston and the park, Walt and grandpa's stories, and that someone (a fox) sneaks into the house at night. Rocco has seen Riot leave during the storm and said nothing.
- **Cold open:** a Friendzy *Truth or Dare* round at the lake. Bash picks dare ("obviously"). Pip reads it out: touch the door of the haunted house. Bash: "Easy." His ears go flat.

- **Warm landing:** they run all the way to the lake. Bash, panting: "I wasn't scared. I was warming up." Pip quietly stays next to him until his paws stop shaking, without saying anything. Bash notices.

- **Mrs. Brook (first appearance):** on her porch with iced tea and wind chimes. Sweet, sharp, funny. She tells them the best summer of her life was "a long time ago, by the lake. Your grandfather made a very good—" She stops. "Lemonade. He made very good lemonade. Drink your tea, dear."

- **The plan:** Riot (it's his lake!) launches "Operation Unbuyable": make the park look so bad Preston gives up. They fake a swamp smell, bring in Bash's whole loud family as "rowdy locals", and Rocco paints a sign: *BEWARE: NATURE*.
- **Preston's beat:** alone for a second at the water's edge, Preston looks at the lake as if he's remembering something, then snaps back. Nobody sees it.
**Clues:** the lantern on the old poster; Preston at the lake; the hiker's "November"; Rocco humming the radio track.

- **The photos:** on the hallway wall, old pictures of grandpa at the lake: grandpa laughing, holding up a paper lantern, a crowd behind him. Pip notices Riot always slows down at that wall. Pip says nothing.
- **Mrs. Brook:** a short cutaway: across the lake, a single candle appears in her window, as it does every storm night.
| World and friendships set up naturally | Lake, apartment, porch light, school, house, park, Mrs. Brook, Walt; every boy gets a spotlight (Riot 1 + 5, Bash 2, Pip 3, Rocco throughout and 5). |

**Arc goal:** the investigation starts for an ordinary reason (saving the park), and it leads straight to Riot's grandfather. The boys learn there used to be a festival with a big game by the lake, that it ended in a storm on 12 August decades ago, and that the town somehow stopped thinking about it. By the end, Riot's friends catch him at the house and he admits he's trying to finish grandpa's last game, but he won't let them help.

**By the end of ep 10 the audience knows:** there was a Lantern Festival with a game night by the lake; grandpa hosted the last one; a storm stopped it on 12 August; nobody in town really remembers it; Riot has a closed wooden box in the house and has been trying to finish "grandpa's game" alone; Rocco knew and kept quiet; Bash practises alone at night; the park might be saved if it's historic.

**Rule for this arc:** the box is only ever seen **closed** (lid: the lake at dusk). Any shot of Riot "playing" is a close-up of a paw, a carved piece or the die, never the board's corners or lantern slots.
- **Festival things** surface in a dusty crate: faded bunting, a folded paper lantern frame (empty, no paper), a hand-drawn sign reading *GAME NIGHT BY THE LAKE*.

- **Walt's story** (one short scene, told while sorting): every summer the town had the Lantern Festival. Everyone played one big game by the lake, families against families, and after each round a lantern went up over the water. "Your grandpa hosted the last one. I was nine. Then the storm came, everyone ran... and somehow we just never did it again. Funny. Nobody ever decided to stop."
- **Hook:** at the bottom of the crate, an envelope of photos. The top one is the storm night: the crowd at the lake, the sky turning. Someone's face at the edge is water-damaged and blurred.

- **The house at night:** real lights-out tension. Footsteps in fours upstairs. Bash, terrified, goes first anyway. They find Riot at a table with a flashlight and a **closed wooden box**, its lid painted with the lake at dusk.

- **Ep 13 "Firefly Night" (Slice + mystery).** The town goes to the lake for the one night the fireflies come. Rocco predicts it to the minute as a joke. Pip drops his nervous act when he thinks nobody's looking: Mrs. Brook sees. Dot knows about the boxes. **Beat:** Mrs. Brook to Pip: "Who are you when nobody's watching, dear?" "Tired." She pats his paw.

**By the end of ep 20 the audience knows:** the festival game was played at the lake; the house only remembers it; the round was never finished; the unfinished round is why it has been one summer for decades. Tier 2 begins.

- **Ep 20 "The Twelfth of August" (Midseason finale).** All four sit in the square for the first time; Bash puts down the die. The house opens up: the whole storm night replays around them, at the lake, with lanterns on the water, the crowd, a banner: LAST LANTERN, LAST DAY OF SUMMER. The storm breaks, everyone runs, the replay stops on the same flash again and again. The board is seen for the first time. It never finished. It's the same storm every year because it's the same year. Pip, alone, understands what ending it means for him.

- **Ep 39 "Twelfth of August" (Finale, part 1).** Festival night. The storm comes on time and the crowd runs. Preston, soaked: "I ran last time." Rocco takes Gus's mic: "This is some guy." He tells the town everything he knows, and for once it stays. All round the lake, porch lights go on. A Friendzy room fills with ten seats, one for each street, with other rooms playing along. Mrs. Brook silently takes the tenth seat. The final round: "Most likely to be the last to realise how important they are to people." Nine votes, all for Mrs. Brook. On her porch, she sees it.

- **Ep 40 "Porch Light Off" (Finale, part 2).** She walks down through the rain with the hatbox. The four take their seats. Bash rolls the die. She and Riot let the lantern go, and the lake fills with light. "You can keep a memory. You can't keep a moment." In the morning: cold air, brown leaves. The hiker is finally agreed with. Pip's family leaves, not far. Game night goes on over Friendzy. A postcard arrives, one line, the postmark smudged. The porch light clicks off, with autumn leaves falling through its last glow.

**By the end of ep 5 the audience knows:** the four boys and their dynamic, the lake, the apartment and the porch light, the "haunted" house, Mrs. Brook, Preston and the park, Walt and grandpa's stories, and that someone (a fox) sneaks into the house at night. Rocco has seen Riot leave during the storm and said nothing.
**Type:** Comedy. **Purpose:** introduce Preston, the Mayor and the save-the-park storyline; Gus's radio and the lo-fi musician; the first hiker gag.

- **Cold open:** a peacock in a very bright suit steps out of a very long car at the park. Preston: "Ladies, gentlemen, ducks. Imagine... this, but more." He unveils a drawing of the park covered in a giant building.

- **The plan:** Riot (it's his lake!) launches "Operation Unbuyable": make the park look so bad Preston gives up. They fake a swamp smell, bring in Bash's whole loud family as "rowdy locals", and Rocco paints a sign: *BEWARE: NATURE*.
- **Emotional beat:** on the tower at sunset, Riot tells Rocco this park is the one place he's never wanted to leave. Rocco: "Then we keep it." Simple, sincere.
- **Hook:** Preston's assistant pins a notice on the town board: the park sale vote. Under it, older paper, half torn: the corner of an old poster with a lantern drawn on it.
| World and friendships set up naturally | Lake, apartment, porch light, school, house, park, Mrs. Brook, Walt; every boy gets a spotlight (Riot 1 + 5, Bash 2, Pip 3, Rocco throughout and 5). |

**Arc goal:** the investigation starts for an ordinary reason (saving the park), and it leads straight to Riot's grandfather. The boys learn there used to be a festival with a big game by the lake, that it ended in a storm on 12 August decades ago, and that the town somehow stopped thinking about it. By the end, Riot's friends catch him at the house and he admits he's trying to finish grandpa's last game, but he won't let them help.

**By the end of ep 10 the audience knows:** there was a Lantern Festival with a game night by the lake; grandpa hosted the last one; a storm stopped it on 12 August; nobody in town really remembers it; Riot has a closed wooden box in the house and has been trying to finish "grandpa's game" alone; Rocco knew and kept quiet; Bash practises alone at night; the park might be saved if it's historic.
**Type:** Comedy. **Purpose:** the park vote; introduce Big Hal; first mention of the festival, as a throwaway that nobody can explain.

- **The meeting** in the old school gym. The boys' presentation ("Why The Park Is Good") collapses in order: slides upside down, Bash's family cheering at the wrong moments, Rocco asleep in the front row.
- **Result:** the vote is postponed. Big Hal to the boys: if the park was ever a festival ground, it might count as historic, and a historic park can't be sold. The boys have a mission.
**Clues:** the park was "only ever used for some old festival"; the town can't remember it; Mrs. Brook leaves.
- **Choice:** Riot wants to sell the festival crate in the yard sale ("it's just junk"). The others insist it's proof for the park. Walt hands the crate to Riot: "Then it's yours."
**Type:** Comedy + mystery. **Purpose:** the boys hunt for proof that the park is historic; the records point to 12 August and something odd about the town's summers.
- **The win:** the programs prove the park was the festival ground for generations. Big Hal says it's enough to make the case at the next vote. The boys celebrate.
| Investigation has a grounded reason | Saving the park: prove it was the festival ground. |
| Decoys | The house (chairs, footsteps), Preston (waving records against the park). |

- **Ep 16 "House Rules" (Comedy).** Riot's laminated rules for the house versus four boys in the dark. The second park vote: historic status holds only if the ground is back in use "before the end of summer". Preston laughs. Rocco doesn't. Footsteps in turns; the boys count them.
**Arc goal:** the town gets its festival back for the sake of the park, not knowing what it's doing. The boys learn how hard the truth is to hold, and how little one boy can do.

- **Ep 21 "Committee" (Comedy).** The boys try to tell the town it's always been summer. The fog eats every attempt; even Walt nods and forgets. Meanwhile the Mayor revives the festival to save the park and sets the date: 12 August. Preston offers to sponsor it.
**Arc goal:** the storylines meet. The game finally moves, the festival nears, the park comes down to one decision, and the boys learn what winning will cost.

- **Ep 32 "Final Offer" (Comedy).** Preston's last and largest offer. The Mayor's indecision peaks. The park is saved only if the festival truly finishes. Big Hal and Bash's family lead a very polite protest. **Beat:** Preston alone at the old stage post, then back to being Preston.

7. **Why the park matters to the plot:** it stays protected only if the ground is back in use "before the end of summer". That's the reason the festival is revived, and the deadline is only met when the round finishes.

sources.excerpt: In Maple Hollow, a small lake-and-forest town of animals, it has been summer for decades and nobody has noticed. Riot, a 20-year-old fox lifeguard, has spent years sneaking into the town's "haunted house" to finish his grandfather's old board game alone, without telling anyone. With his roommate Rocco and their younger friends Bash and Pip, a summer of game nights, dumb plans and small mysteries slowly turns into the discovery that the game is holding the whole town in one endless summer. It can only be finished together. Finishing it means autumn arrives, and with it, Pip moves away.

In Maple Hollow, a small lake-and-forest town of animals, it has been summer for decades and nobody has noticed. Riot, a 20-year-old fox lifeguard, has spent years sneaking into the town's "haunted house" to finish his grandfather's old board game alone, without telling anyone. With his roommate Rocco and their younger friends Bash and Pip, a summer of game nights, dumb plans and small mysteries slowly turns into the discovery that the game is holding the whole town in one endless summer. It can only be finished together. Finishing it means autumn arrives, and with it, Pip moves away.
